utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good afternoon to everyone. Mr. Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon Your Honours; good afternoon to everyone in the courtroom. This is case number IT-06-90-T, The Prosecutor versus Ante Gotovina et al.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. Mr. Waespi, are you ready to continue your examination-in-chief? Mr. Mirkovic, I'd like it remind you that the solemn declaration you gave yesterday that you would speak the truth, the whole truth and nothing but the truth, still binds you. That may be clear to you. Mr. Waespi.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. I have about ten or 15 more minutes to complete my examination in chief.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Mirkovic.

utterances.speaker: SAVA MIRKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good afternoon to all.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Yesterday we ended with you telling the Judges why your family left on the 4th of August, 1995. Can you tell us whether it was a difficult decision for you to leave?

utterances.speaker: SAVA MIRKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not only for me, but for everyone who loses everything that you have earned for ages and centuries and then you lose if in one day. When we left we had no idea where we were going and where we would end up. And this -- since the moment when we arrived in Serbia up to this day we are just wandering around the world. In other words, we lost everything, we have never been able to recover any of the property we used to have and as for the younger folk, they weren't able to get a job; for the older folk, they weren't able to have a pension and to get anything was very difficult.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: You said in your statement that is now in evidence that you heard Mr. Tudjman talking over the radio. Can you briefly reiterate what you recall him saying?

utterances.speaker: SAVA MIRKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I heard this on the radio, Radio Zagreb, he was calling on the Serbian people. He was saying that they shouldn't fear anything that they will be tried, that they will be given a fair trial. That's what he said. And there was repeated throughout the day, while we were still there. And of course people did not believe that they would get a fair day in court, so they did not remain there.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: So you just said you did not believe what Mr. Tudjman was saying.

utterances.speaker: SAVA MIRKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: And why not?

utterances.speaker: SAVA MIRKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mentioned already, you probably know the history of that region you know what happened in World War II with the orthodox population there and even after that when I told you what happened in Miljevci in the Medak pocket in Western Slavonia, so knowing all that, how could you just stay there, and await this army to arrive, because we knew that all those people who did stay and waited, they did not fair well. This actually happened to my mother, and she remained there, and the first days when the soldiers arrived there they kept saying don't worry just feed your cattle and so on but then eight days later, someone who did not like this whole thing came along and did what he did.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: What is the name of your mother?

utterances.speaker: SAVA MIRKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Her name is Djurdjia Mirkovici. Her maiden name was Ivakic. She was born in 1925.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: And what exactly do you know that happened to her?

utterances.speaker: SAVA MIRKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I arrived Serbia, I tried to telephone some friends in Split. But it was impossible to get through, so that after a while, finally we did manage to get in touch. I got in touch with the late Dusan Mirkovic; I think he died about a year and a half ago, and I asked him all he told me was I went to your house, she was killed, she was dowsed with something black and set on fire. This was the first information I learned. He said that he had told Jovo Mirkovic and Mijo Lazic who were in the Lora prison to bury her remains when they go home. So when Jovo came from the prison, and Smilja, his wife, I got in touch with them; I found them in Bosansko Novo Selo where they gave a statement to your investigators, and she was the one who told me about how -- what transpired and how everything went and I can repeat what she told me in 1995, if you like.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Yes. Before you do that --

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Mr. President, the two persons that were mentioned by the witness, Jovo and Smilja Mirkovic they gave also witnesses statements to the ICTY and they have been admitted by you as 92 bis statements. The statement of Jovo Mirkovic is P628 and the statement of Smiljana Mirkovic is P629.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Mr. Mirkovic, yes, if you can please recall what you were told about the death of your mother.

utterances.speaker: SAVA MIRKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not only can I recall, I can recall every detail, because this is something you cannot really forget. She told me that there were at home those days, that they fed the cattle that was left behind, because most people had left the village. Until the 12th of August, as she recounted it, that morning, they were outside in the -- in the yard outside my home when two soldiers arrived. They weren't coming along the road. They came across the fields and jumped over fences, and one of them just started shooting. He, as she recounted, according to what she told me, he start shooting from about a distance of ten meters. My mother fell immediately and the woman, the one who told me about, she fainted. She also fell down. So after a while, when she came to, she realized that she hadn't been hit. Maybe they weren't -- they didn't mean to hit her. Then she realized that my mother was dead. She was lying underneath her. So then she went to a neighbour's home to tell him what happened to my mother, and then he left the Mirkovici hamlet and went to Podinarje where some 25 to 30 people were who had sought shelter, there figuring that no Croatian soldier would go there. When Jovan Mirkovic came out of the prison, he told me this was about the 21st of August, he told me that he went there, with Mijo Lazic and his son Dusan. He worked in Porice. So he was telling me that they -- we entered your house, not everything had been looted. We found some blankets and we put in the blankets whatever bones remained there, because her whole body was not intact. Probably it had been burned, but also maybe some animals just took the bones away, and they buried the body, the remains that they found, they buried in the yard by the well, the water well.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Mirkovic. Do you know whether people returned to the hamlet of Mirkovici?

utterances.speaker: SAVA MIRKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: So are there any persons living now in Mirkovici?

utterances.speaker: SAVA MIRKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No one lives in Mirkovici.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President, I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Waespi. Mr. Misetic you will be the first one to cross-examine the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Mirkovic, you will now be cross-examined by Mr. Misetic, who is counsel for Mr. Gotovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Mirkovic.

utterances.speaker: SAVA MIRKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good afternoon to you, too.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Mirkovic let me start off by asking you about your trip on the evening of the 4th, your flight from your village of Mirkovici. Did you have any physical impediments on the night of the 4th that hindered your ability to leave towards Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: SAVA MIRKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were no impediments. At least not on the roads when we started off. We took off about 9.30/10.00 p.m. There were no roadblocks.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I think you may have misunderstood my question. Did you physically have any physical ailments that hindered your ability to travel on the night of the 4th.

utterances.speaker: SAVA MIRKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Was your vision good?

utterances.speaker: SAVA MIRKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What do you mean? My vision was good then and it's still good.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Your legs were okay, your back is okay.

utterances.speaker: SAVA MIRKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, thank God.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: The next question I had is your witness statement identifies your father as being named Djuradj is that the formal name for Djuro?

utterances.speaker: SAVA MIRKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Djuradj is his name.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Was he known as Djuro?

utterances.speaker: SAVA MIRKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Now, if I could call up Mr. Registrar 1D44-0192, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Mirkovic, this is a supplemental information sheet that was prepared by the Office of the Prosecutor after you spoke with Mr. Waespi, on your arrival here in The Hague. It contains additional information clarifying portions of your witness statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: If we could turn the page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Mirkovic, is that your signature on the second page?

utterances.speaker: SAVA MIRKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Does this supplemental information sheet accurately reflect what you told the Office of the Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: SAVA MIRKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I told the truth.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: And, Mr. Mirkovic --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. -- Mr. Misetic, I see an English text and I'd like to have verified in which way the witness has been able to review the text as we see it here in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: The practice is that we read these notes back to the witness in English, and correct whatever the witness tells us and then once the process is completed, the witness signs it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You read it in English to the witnesses.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Yes. But we have an interpreter who translation --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... so it is orally interpret what had you read to him.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And then he signs it on the basis of the interpretation given to him.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you for that information. Please proceed, Mr. Misetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: If I were to ask you the same questions that you were asked when Mr. Waespi was interviewing you and preparing this supplemental information sheet, would your answers be the same today as they were when you gave these answers to Mr. Waespi a few days ago?

utterances.speaker: SAVA MIRKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. They can only be the same.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would tender this supplemental information sheet as an additional 92 ter statement of the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Waespi.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: No objections.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No objections. In view of the positions taken by the parties, we -- the Chamber is very likely to take a position to admit, but we have not -- at least I have not seen any copy of it, a hard copy of it. It's not tendered so usually before taking an admission under 92 ter we'd like to read the whole of the statement rather than just have a glance of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: I do have a few hard copies.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, if you'd give them to us and we can proceed on the basis that there is an likelihood in view of the positions taken by the parties that the Chamber will admit the document. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Could we get a MFI for that, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that becomes Exhibit number D327, marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Mirkovic --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: It is it important that the Bench have a copy of this if I wish to ask you questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: In the second paragraph of this supplemental information sheet, you say that when you gave your witness statement to the investigators of the Office of the Prosecutor on the 9th of March, 2007, you were sitting together with Jovo and Smilja Mirkovic. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SAVA MIRKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we were.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: And when Jovo and Smilja Mirkovic were giving their statements to the investigators of the Office of the Prosecutor you were present in the room with them as well. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SAVA MIRKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know whether -- what time you mean, because the investigators came to Bosansko Novo Selo twice, on two occasions and on the second occasion I wasn't there. I was only there on the 9th of March.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: So when Jovo and Smilja Mirkovic gave their statements on the 9th of March 2007 you were present in the room. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SAVA MIRKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: In your supplemental information sheet you say, "Although I was trying to refresh their memory because they were older people I did not try to influence them in any way." Now, can you tell the Court specifically which portions of the testimony of Jovo and Smiljana you assisted them by refreshing their memory?

utterances.speaker: SAVA MIRKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was no -- nothing specific because they started telling their story from the end. They weren't very focussed, and I just told them then, Do you recall what he told me in 1995? Is that how it happened, and they said yes. So it wasn't that I really had to refresh their memory. They could remember all of that, but it was a bit difficult for them, because a lot of time has elapsed and these were older people. They are sick, ill, and even a bit senile. So they weren't really -- their memories weren't really all that great.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: So if I understand you correctly at certain time you would say, Don't you remember you told me this, and they would say simply say, Yes. Is that how it went?

utterances.speaker: SAVA MIRKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, nothing more.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Do you remember specifically how many times you said, Do you remember that you told me this, and they would say, Yes?

utterances.speaker: SAVA MIRKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't really recall. Maybe twice or three times. I don't really recall.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Do you remember what the topic was, when you said, Do you remember you told me this, and they said, Yes?

utterances.speaker: SAVA MIRKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that I told Jovo when he started telling the investigators about this event, instead of telling them about what happened and how he buried the remains of my mother, he started telling them, You know, they chased me, they beat me, and so on and then I told him, Wait a minute Jovo just tell them about what they came for to hear and then you can tell them about the rest or for, instances, Smilja said the two of them came, they were in uniform these two soldiers, one of them started shooting, I fell over Djuka. After this I got up and then I asked her, Well, what do you mean you got up? You remember you told me that you had fainted, because that is what she had told me and then she just confirmed she said, yes, that ask how it went. So there is nothing special. Because the way she said -- or the way she recalled the way she told these things it seemed as if she was just lying over my mother and then she got up and left but that is not really how it really went, because they were at the time they were at the high school building that's where they were taken, that's where they were sheltered and that's where she told me about this, but then because so many years had elapsed in the meantime and because of all of the problems that they had had in the mean time she couldn't really recall all the details; but there was nothing really important in the reminding.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Do you recall the names of the investigators that were there?

utterances.speaker: SAVA MIRKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was Mr. -- I think his name was Steven; he said he was from Australia, and another gentleman, I can't -- I can't really remember that other name. Because these weren't, you know, our names that I would recall easily.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Now, did either one of the investigators at any point of the interview of Smiljana and Jovo tell you that you shouldn't try to assist the witnesses in refreshing their recollection?

utterances.speaker: SAVA MIRKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They said you needn't tell them anything you should just tell them what you know, and that's what they did.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: At what point in the interview did the investigators tell you that you needn't tell them anything?

utterances.speaker: SAVA MIRKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right at the very start. I tried to draw their attention to their previous accounts at the very outset.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Let me move on to a different topic. Mr. Mirkovic, in your 2007 statement at paragraph 1 you say: I "Thought there may be an attack by the Croatian army and the Serbian soldiers may be defending us."

utterances.speaker: SAVA MIRKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Why did you think that the Serbian soldiers would be defending you?

utterances.speaker: SAVA MIRKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't quite understand, sir. Are we supposed to talk about that, are we supposed to discuss my mother's death? Are we now going back to the attack or shall we go on discussing my mother's death? There were people who were under attack. I suppose there should be someone defending them, right?

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Where were they defending you from, what positions?

utterances.speaker: SAVA MIRKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, I don't know what positions those were because there was no one defending. You see that's why we are here because there was no one to protect us.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Well, on the morning of the 4th, at 4.55 a.m., where did you think the Serbian soldiers were from what positions on the morning of the 4th did you think they were defending you?

utterances.speaker: SAVA MIRKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know sir. I don't know where they were. You should ask someone who was in charge of the military. I didn't know. I'm here to testify about one thing and you're asking me about something different altogether. I'm no specialist in strategy; therefore, I could hardly be expected to tell you anything about this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Mirkovic, from your last two answers it appears that you had little, if any, knowledge about military matters. Nevertheless, Mr. Misetic, when -- since you said that you -- you would expected some Defence is entitled to ask you questions about that, this does not in any way shift the -- the substance of your testimony away from what you considered to be an important matter, especially for you, which is quite understandable. Nevertheless, Mr. Misetic is entitled to ask you these questions, and to the extent you have knowledge of the matters he asks you, please tell us. If you have no knowledge of it, please tell us that you do not know. Please proceed, Mr. Misetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can't say I know nothing because we all knew that on one side there was the Serb army the army of the Republic of Serbian Krajina, on the other side there was the army of the Republic of Croatia. Everyone knew that, and that is the extent of my knowledge, too. Those who were shelling us were the ones we fled and then we want to the move on to Bosnia, perhaps or Serbia, and that's why we started out that way. And that is much as I know, where were they, now, that is something that I can't say.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Mirkovic, you also say in paragraph 1: "We were under the protection of the United Nations and I believed that nobody could attack us." Why did you think that you couldn't be attacked because of the United Nations?

utterances.speaker: SAVA MIRKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, because this area was the responsibility of the UN or the international community. We had every confidence that the UN would achieve some sort of peaceful solution in the area and that people would not come to any great harm. We'd also heard that some representatives of the Republic of the Serbian Krajina several days before had been off to some talks in Geneva that is something that was broadcast on Radio Zagreb on Radio Srpska Krajina, Radio Belgrade, Belgrade TV, or whatever you chose to call them. We, the people, were hearing such things at the time there were talks under way they were trying to achieve some sort of peaceful solution, and we didn't expect that anyone would go attacking us during the talks.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Mirkovic, at paragraph 4 of your statement you indicate that the people could not go to Bosansko Grahovo because it had already been taken over by the Croatian army so they were moving through Lika, through Srb and further on. You were aware were you not on the morning of the 4th, that the Croatian army had taken Grahovo the week before?

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: I do have a B/C/S copy for the witness because it is not on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: That's fine -- oh, sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, if you -- I think it is it good if the witness has an opportunity to read the portion of this statement you're referring to. Please proceed, Mr. Misetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Do you see at paragraph 4, sir, that you say that the people could not go to Bosansko Grahovo because it had already been taken over by the Croatian army? The question is you were aware on the 4th of August that the Croatian army had launched an attack and had seized Bosansko Grahovo the week before. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SAVA MIRKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: And you were aware that Mr. Martic had issued a general mobilisation order at the end of July 1995, after the fall of Grahovo. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SAVA MIRKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't know about that at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Mirkovic, on the 4th of August, 1995, you would have been 35 years old. Were you ever in the army of the Republika of Srpska Krajina?

utterances.speaker: SAVA MIRKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had been mobilized, just like everyone else.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: What were the dates of your mobilisation?

utterances.speaker: SAVA MIRKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: It doesn't have to be specific dates. Months -- can you give us months that you were mobilized, years?

utterances.speaker: SAVA MIRKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was an on-and-off thing. I sometimes had to go.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Were you a mobilized soldier of the army of the Republika Srpska Krajina on the 4th of August, 1995?

utterances.speaker: SAVA MIRKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I was at home at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, if I could call up, please, 1D44-0194.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Mirkovic, this is a document seized by Croatian authorities after the fall of the Republika Srpska Krajina in the archive of the army of the Republika Srpska Krajina, there's a list of junior officers of the army of the Republika Srpska Krajina.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: If we could turn the page, please. In the B/C/S if we could turn the page, and if we could leave that in English. Your Honour it is a 40-page document; we have only translated the first page and the relevant page. I have the full 40 pages, though, in case any needs -- I think we have produced it to the Prosecution in case they want to look through it. I don't know if the Bench wants to see it but ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Waespi.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Yes, I'm fine with this -- this excerpt.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Mirkovic, at number 419 of the list of junior officers of the ARSK is a Mirkovic, Savo, son of Djure, born in 1960. Is that you?

utterances.speaker: SAVA MIRKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know if this is me. But name is definitely not Savo. My name is Sava.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Were you an officer of the army of the Republika Srpska Krajina?

utterances.speaker: SAVA MIRKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Do you know anybody named Savo Mirkovic, son of Djure, born in 1960?

utterances.speaker: SAVA MIRKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'd ask that this exhibit be marked, and I tender it into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar. Perhaps, yes, I do agree, Mr. Waespi that usually I give an opportunity first to --

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Yes. No objection but I would love to see the cover page of the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I think --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... it's on my screen -- what is not on our -- the original cover page. Mr. Misetic, nevertheless, the cover page doesn't give any information about the date of the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I understand that, Your Honour. That is the way the document is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, yes so you can't provide us further information.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No. Any other details about this document which would make it easier for us to understand what it actually is.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I can provide the source -- the date the document was taken, the place that it was taken.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... of course after -- after the early day the of August, 1995, then -- I take it it was not -- it was not found before Operation Storm.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Correct, correct. That is correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And that is, Mr. Waespi, I take it, you would -- if it seized by the Croatian authorities as -- there's a logical expectation that it would not be in their hands before Operation Storm.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Yes, the document says what it says. The little we have seen, the witness said what he had to say about the -- his name.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's content.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: We don't have any objections to the document itself.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that becomes exhibit number D721.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D721 is admitted into evidence. But it is cover page and one page, including number 419. But I saw very quickly another page, which seemed to be not exactly the same as the cover page, or was I -- are there any other pages which are not just giving names, but I think I very briefly saw something. Perhaps the last page.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes, I think we just attached -- we did first the cover page, the page that's relevant for this witness and the last page of this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I remember that I had seen another page. So it is now a three-page document. And if we could see also the last page. Is this the last page?

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: That is the last page, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Mirkovic, I asked you some questions about your health at the beginning. You were a healthy 35-year-old male on the 4th of August, 1995. How is it that the army of the Republika Srpska Krajina didn't mobilize you prior to Operation Storm?

utterances.speaker: SAVA MIRKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, not everyone was mobilized.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Again, how is it that you weren't mobilized? Did you receive a mobilization call-up?

utterances.speaker: SAVA MIRKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I told you it was an on-and-off thing with me. I would be mobilized at times. When I wasn't mobilized, I spent my time at home. I explained to the gentleman how much we believed in our survival in the area and what faith we had in the UN. We put up tents with my neighbour, we put up tables and staged a whole wedding for 100 people. That's how great our confidence was.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: From the 28th of July, 1995, to the 4th of August, 1995, did you receive a mobilisation call-up?

utterances.speaker: SAVA MIRKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember. I don't think so though.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Now, with respect to President Tudjman's call, it is in your statement and you repeated it again today apparently one of the things that stood out to about his statement was the fact that President Tudjman said that people would get a fair trial. On the 4th of August, were you aware that you could be tried for treason by Croatian authorities?

utterances.speaker: SAVA MIRKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's not what I was thinking about at the time, not at all. I didn't expect to be tried by anyone. I didn't expect there to be any trials. Why would anyone try me or anyone else? I committed no crime. I was a victim of a crime.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I'm asking you, sir, you were -- you were asked some questions about your decision to leave on the 4th of August, and having been a participant in the army of the Republika Srpska Krajina you were aware, were you not, that that would be considered an act of treason by Croatian authorities. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SAVA MIRKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not aware of anything, treason or no treason. This simply isn't what was on my mind at that time. My mother was no soldier. Look what became of her. Did anyone call her a traitor?

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Mirkovic, were you aware at the time that you could be tried for anything by Croatian authorities?

utterances.speaker: SAVA MIRKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Why would I have been tried by anyone?

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, if we could call up, please, 1D44-0188.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Mirkovic, what I'm showing you now is an aerial satellite view of Polace. You said in your supplemental information sheet you describe the fact that Polace is comprised of several hamlets. That is in paragraph 4 of your supplemental information sheet. We have circled many of the hamlets in Polace, and as you can see on the map, your village of Mirkovici is that the location of where Mirkovici is?

utterances.speaker: SAVA MIRKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: If you look there are now two rather large shaped objects. The one to the right we have marked Velika Polace; the one to the left we have marked Mala Polace. Are you familiar with the terms Velika and Mala Polace?

utterances.speaker: SAVA MIRKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I explained about that yesterday. Velika Polace, Mala Polace. All the hamlets that we looked at yesterday on that map. That whole lot makes up Polace. This covers an extensive area. The area ranges from the Knin-Split road and then through Biskupija up to Kijevo, Mount Dinara and Kozijak [phoen]. These are the four borders as it were, so it is an extensive area covered by that village. It's a large village.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Do you see the area to the right that is marked Sivo Brdo?

utterances.speaker: SAVA MIRKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Do you recognise that as a location of the area known as Sivo Brdo?

utterances.speaker: SAVA MIRKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is also quite an extensive area, the one that people refer to as Sivo Brdo as a matter of principle this should not be south of Lazici because that is what the map shows. This is Lazici and this is Sivo Brdo; it should be behind Lazici but Sivo Brdo should be above Lazici, Mirkovici, and Cinguri [phoen]; and that is the area this mountain range in a manner of speaking that is normally referred to as Sivo Brdo.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: May I ask the court usher to actually mark on the map what he perceives as Sivo Brdo.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Misetic, at the same time, we have to be very careful because places are identified primarily by what you have marked on this map and I take it you did this to the best of your abilities. At the same time, the -- as appears from the witness answers he can locate matters relatively but whether this is the middle of France or the area you say it is, of course, is without thorough studying of the details of such a map, of course are rather adventurous exercise. I hope you are aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Is the issue whether this is in fact the area of Polace?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I take it you have chosen that. But to ask the witness to say where is this, this, this, and this, this, that then of course the witness has not found it on the map as you did it. He sees it and whether it is again the middle of France or the middle of Germany or the place you say it is, which I'm quite inclined to accept it is, requires something I would not expect a witness to be able to do immediately.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: If can I ask a few more questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm just putting it this to you. Yes or look at some more details or for example to zoom in on Mirkovici and see whether he recognized the shape of the roads and then [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: That's what I was going to ask, if he recognises the road that starts from the upper left-hand corner and goes down towards the middle of the page and then goes back up to the right and then comes back down.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But then of course a road of this shape you find that in -- could we prepares first zoom in and see with what precision we can look at Mirkovici and to see whether the witness recognises by the shape, the position of the houses, at least one point on this map so that we have a better anchor --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: That's fine Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: For the --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll have to try and find out whether --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Can we zoom it in a little more?

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Mirkovic, are you able to identify by looking at this whether this is in fact Mirkovici?

utterances.speaker: SAVA MIRKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm a bit uncertain about this map. Can you tell me about this blue line? Is this the Split-Knin road or is that the other one?

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: The blue line is something that we drew in to show -- you should ignore that. That is showing Velika Polace. The road you are talking about, I believe, if I can orient the witness, the Split-Knin road is to the left, that road that goes from the middle of the left-hand side of the page --

utterances.speaker: SAVA MIRKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The white line, right?

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... towards the top of the page?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could we ask the witness perhaps with the assistance of the usher or by using the cursor to tell us where he thinks the road is which he just mentioned. So not to mark it, but for the time being just to -- Witness -- perhaps you guide the witness, Mr. Misetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Mirkovic, do you recognise -- this is quite a zoom-in, so I'm not sure he's going to be able to recognize it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... you can zoom out, zoom it out back.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes we can zoom in and out as --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Mirkovic --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, I think we should leave it and -- leave it as a whole.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Because it a bigger area [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could we have the whole of the -- yes, this picture.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Do you see the Knin-Drnis road or the Knin-Split road?

utterances.speaker: SAVA MIRKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Knin-Drnis. I didn't get that part. What we're looking at is the Knin-Split road and then on through Polace, the hamlet of Maglovi that is the middle of Polace and then we move on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One second, please. Would it not as evidence of -- of the map but rather as evidence of what the witness apparently recognizes on this map ask him to mark with the marker where he thinks on this map we find the --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: That's fine. Knin-Split road.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Knin-Split road and then always have to remind the colours is blue for the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could the witness be given a blue pen and could he mark on this map where he recognizes or where he sees the Knin-Split road. Yes, please, you can do it on the screen and then it will appear.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is the Split-Knin road it forks off to the right here for the hamlet of Mirkovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And could you tell us what the Knin direction and what is the Split direction? If you put a K at the end of the line which in the direction of Knin; and for Split, it would be ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Knin is this way, and Split is this way.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I was just trying to verify to what extent it was a good comprehension of what is on the screen, Mr. Misetic. May I take it that -- do you need further markings?

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes, one more.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Mirkovic, if you could circle the area that is it called Sivo Brdo?

utterances.speaker: SAVA MIRKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Circle it? It is a rather broad area and concept to, Sivo Brdo. I will try to show it to you. That's as far as I know. That's what older people used to tell me. These were Sivo Brdo.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: For the record, the witness drew a half-circle to the right-hand side of the page to indicate Sivo Brdo.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Mirkovic, based on your knowledge if someone were on Sivo Brdo and wanted to go to Knin would they have to take the Knin-Split road and go past Mirkovici?

utterances.speaker: SAVA MIRKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you please repeat that what do you mean someone is in Sivo Brdo?

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Hypothetically, if I were in a car and I went as far as I could up Sivo Brdo and decided from there now I want to go to Knin by road, which road would I have to take?

utterances.speaker: SAVA MIRKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's not like there was a road out there. It was a dirt track for tractors, maybe small vehicles, but not passenger vehicles, not nice cars, but you could take the road through Lazici, Mirkovici, and though Bukvet. I don't see Bukvet here, it's just a small hamlet Bukvet to Borovici, Ranici. There's a whole group of those. People made roads themselves. They would go to the woods they would take their cattle there, that sort of thing.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Misetic may I ask you one question, I heard a couple of time in English translation a pronunciation of Siva Brda rather than Sivo Brdo. Is there any way or singular or plural --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Sivo Brdo is one; Siva Brda are the mountains, so it would be [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That might I'm trying to understand. I noticed this and I also noticed that the difference is not for example if you look at page 24, line 22/23 the plural is these were and then it appears Sivo Brdo which apparently is the singular.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: It is correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Whereas in the words were spoken as.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Siva Brda.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Siva Brda so that might also explain some of the confusion and some of the corrections.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that's clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Thank you. If we could just leave this on the screen for a moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Was there a, and I will use the B/C/S word and the English word because there's some difficulty in the translation, I believe a zadruga, which is spelled Z-A-D-R-U-G-A or in English, the best we could come up with was cooperative hall in Mala Polace, that you're aware of? Do you know where the zadruga was there Mala Polace?

utterances.speaker: SAVA MIRKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There were several different places those were just shops.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Were you familiar with the zadruga in Maglovi?

utterances.speaker: SAVA MIRKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, there wasn't one in Maglovi. I think it was right in the middle of the village where the monument was, the culture hall. It was right between the two hamlets Maglova and Milivojevici.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Would that be between within the --

utterances.speaker: SAVA MIRKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Where you wrote Maglovi. This road to Knin, to the left where it says Maglovi that is Maglovi to the right heading towards Knin that is Milivojevici.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: So would the cooperative hall have been on the right-hand side of the road in Milivojevici?

utterances.speaker: SAVA MIRKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I'm telling you is this, between Maglova and Milivojevici between these two hamlets, you can't say it was on neither side specifically. It was right in the middle.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Are you aware of a meeting that took place in that meeting, the zadruga in that area on the 4th of August that was held between representatives of the hamlets of Polace and the civil defence of the RSK?

utterances.speaker: SAVA MIRKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: First I hear of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Well, you said in one of your statements - let me find it - paragraph 6 of your 2007 statement. You say: "We were not told to leave. However, later friends told me there were teams of people coming to some villages around Knin telling people to pack up and evacuate." Can you explain a little bit who you heard this from, and what you heard?

utterances.speaker: SAVA MIRKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When we arrived Serbia some people arrived three days later, some five, some 20, it was an arduous journey before we got there; and then we would meet people a month later, six months later. We would talk about what had become of us, how we left and who had told them, and I can't remember specifically but I know for sure that around [indiscernible] there was a group, or at least that is what we were told at the time meaning I didn't hear this myself, that people were being evacuated and were leaving. I said we were at home. Nobody told us anything we didn't know and now we realized that people from Cetina, Civljane, and Vrlika were leaving and they were taking this road that you marked. We from our hamlet were looking at this. The distance being perhaps 400 meters, 200 or 250 meters as the crow flies.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm going to have to clarify something because I believe the witness mentioned Maglovi in the answer and it is not in the transcript so I would like to follow up with him on that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: In your last answer, Mr. Mirkovic, you mentioned that people told you about something in Maglovi. Can you clarify that, please, because it wasn't picked up by the transcript.

utterances.speaker: SAVA MIRKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't quite understand. What do you want me to say about Maglovi? Whether I said that?

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I believe you had said something to the effect of that you heard that people had been in Maglovi and had said something --

utterances.speaker: SAVA MIRKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, I didn't say that. It just seemed that way to you. You just heard it that way.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I will tender this exhibit. This is an page after this, which I do not need now based on the witness's answers so I will tender the exhibit that is marked.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Before doing so, would there be an opportunity, the witness has told us several times about Milivojevici.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And could we invite the witness to mark with a letter M where he finds Milivojevici on this map. Do I then understand that Milivojevici is in the same area although at the other side of the road, compared to Maglovi?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you for that. And -- yes. That makes it clear for me.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: No objection, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No objections. Map, one page marked by the witness, Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that becomes exhibit number D722.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D722 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Mirkovic, did you hear at any point about a meeting that was held in the zadruga in Milivojevici in which the civil Defence told the leaders of the hamlets to evacuate the civilian population?

utterances.speaker: SAVA MIRKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, never. This is the first time that I hear of it, from you. Because these people there would have loved had someone told them you know you should pick up and leave because this and this is going to happen, but nothing of that sort happened, and this is the first time that I hear of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Now, in your statement, as I mentioned before you said that people couldn't go through Grahovo but instead went through Lika to Srb and further on. Why would people want to go to Grahovo?

utterances.speaker: SAVA MIRKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The reason I mentioned that was to describe which way we took, because if you were heading towards Bosnia, everyone was going Knin, Grahovo, Drvar, Petrovac, and Banja Luka, that direction. No one went by Lika. That is it the only reason I mentioned that. There was no other reason.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: If we could put the map that the witness marked back on the screen, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Did you see ARSK forces on the evening of the 4th or the morning of the 5th in and around the area of Polace?

utterances.speaker: SAVA MIRKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't see, I just saw these columns of tractors and trucks and cars, convoys people were walking. There was no army anywhere, and people were wondering where the army was in fact. There was no one, no military, no one.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar may I call up 1D04-0043, please. This is again for the benefit of the Trial Chamber, the book of the RSK General Milisav Sekulic. This is an excerpt, begins at page -- sorry. 192 and 193 in the original. 1D44-012 in the English and 1D44-0042 for the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could all the microphones but the witness's please be switched off.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: We can start at the bottom.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: This is General Sekulic reporting on the activities of General Milan Celeketic on Nebojsa Popovic commander of the 1st Light Vrlika Brigade on the 4th of August. And in the English, I think it should be -- towards the top of the English, please. In the English. Oh, sorry, towards the bottom of the English; I apologise and it is the section that begins under number 3 in the B/C/S. No, sorry, above number 3. Talks about General Celeketic appointed Captain Popovic as commander of the 1st Light Brigade Vrlika and continues on down: "The enemy artillery relentlessly pounded the territory of Vrlika municipality not knowing what was happening on the Dinara axis, Captain Popovic went to the forward line of defence on Dinara and issued tasks for defence on reserve posts. At night between 4 and 5 August ..."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. --

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: I think the B/C/S is obviously the previous page, number 2.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes it came into my mind as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: 4th and 5th of August. Yes, we will have to move up to the top of the page in B/C/S to see whether. No it seems not --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Enemy artillery is it the -- [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Enemy artillery.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I will start at enemy artillery.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, because you started earlier higher up.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Fine.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: "The enemy artillery relentlessly pounded the territory of Vrlika municipality. Not knowing what was happening on the Dinara axis, Captain Popovic went to the forward line of defence on Dinara and issued tasks for defence on Dinara and issued tasks for defence on reserve posts. At night between 4 and 5 August, the brigade pulled out to Polace, Sivo Brdo," and that is it a Z in the English and if you look in the B/C/S, Your Honours, it is should be Polace. That's an error. "Most of the men willfully abandoned the brigade and went to their homes to get their families. The remaining troops were retreating with the equipment toward Knin but due to lack of fuel, they left the vehicles and therefore the equipment. Popovic arrived in Petrovac with part of the command, weapons and equipment via Padjene and Srb." Now, if we can go back now to the map, the previous exhibit that was admitted into evidence. Now, according to General Celeketic's book recounting the statement of Captain Popovic, on the evening of the 4th and the morning of the 5th he pulled out the first Light Infantry Brigade Vrlika to Sivo Brdo. And then evacuated his equipment, at least portions of his equipment and personnel out to Knin and on to Petrovac. You were there on the evening of the 4th in Mirkovici, you saw ARSK troops in and around Sivo Brdo, did you not?

utterances.speaker: SAVA MIRKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We did not see anyone and we can't really see anyone from Mirkovici because it is in a depression as compared to Sivo Brdo which was higher up so we couldn't see anyone; and I don't see why you are reading something that someone wrote in a book, because from 1990 onwards when the events in Yugoslavia broke out, no one has written the truth about Yugoslavia, so I don't understand what you're read to go me. This man wrote the book to sell it. Because wouldn't it be nice if people only wrote the truth and not just anything in order to sell the book, regardless of whether that really transpired or not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Mirkovic, the book has been written. It describes a situation close to your village, and Mr. Misetic can ask questions about it and if you say, and that's how I understand your answer to be, This is not what I saw, then I'm not convinced that what the book says is the truth, then please -- please focus on what you have seen, what you have heard, and don't bother too much on why people may write things that are not all the -- in accordance with the truth and why Mr. Misetic asks these questions to you. Please proceed, Mr. Misetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I will tender -- one moment, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, the last time we used portions of this book we told the Court that we would translate several chapters through it through CLSS. That has now been done. We have the -- I think it is three chapters of the book translated. They are here. Portions of it have been used before but for ease of reference in the future we would tender all three chapters of it so we don't have to admit portions of the book at various stages.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Waespi.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Obviously there is a thin link to the witness but as a bar table motioning, I don't have an objection.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's not discuss at this moment the weight of the document. There are later stages where this can be done. Of course my hesitation at this moment is that we admit into evidence apparently quite a volume of evidence, which of course we haven't seen, but since there's no --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Actually, if can I correct that. We have gone through many portions of this translation through a protected witness, if the Court will recall, several portions of the chapters are not translated. It just now all been put in three chapters.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I was not aware that the total volume would not be larger because you are also referring to what we might expect in the future.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: That is also the case, but we'll refer back to it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: It occurs to me, Your Honour, that the practice with the bar table submissions has been to indicate those particular portions or aspects of the submission that are relevant, both to guide the Court and the parties which would make our job easier in going through the volume of material. I don't mean to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, what happens Mr. Tieger is quite surprising. Mr. Misetic introduces a book through a witness, and other portions of that book have been introduced through witnesses as well. Since Mr. Waespi now uses the word I consider it a bar table, you immediately now switch to what is the guidance of the Chamber for really bar table evidence, that is evidence which is not introduced through a witness but just on itself, that all apparently as a result of Mr. Waespi's comment that link with this witness was thin, and where Mr. Misetic has explained to us that there are links with other witnesses as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I leave that to the Court, Your Honour and I didn't mean to focus on a formality. That wasn't the issue, it is just in the context of bar table submissions it seemed a way to aide both the parties and the Court in identifying what might otherwise appear to be voluminous material at least navigating its way through there. If it is not helpful here, that is no problem. If it seems like a useful approach to larger volumes of material I suggest it for that purpose.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I am more or less in the air at this moment because I haven't seen it. I don't know exactly what total volume is. I don't know of what is now presented has been dealt with earlier through other witnesses or through this witness. If the parties would be in a position to together to look at what is now presented, what chapters, and then give a shared description of what these chapters are about in if not in one-liners then perhaps in two-liners so that we have the guidance, and, at the same time it is not the same as the purely bar table evidence which we discussed before and for which we gave guidance.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I could just respond. First, this is far from a bar table submission. There are various points that were actually led on direct by the Prosecution regarding military targets on the 4th, regarding presence of troops on the road, whether there were any military in the area, et cetera, whether a witness agrees with the Defence is not -- on a document in cross-examination is not the test to see whether it is admissible or whether it is bar table. If I could also just add this one point. None of the chapters that we are tendering are things that were not previously tendered. We can pull the Defence exhibit numbers that have been admitted. All we're doing is taking the chapters that deal specifically with Operation Storm, putting them in one place so that we can refer back to them instead three pages here, five pages here, et cetera; and quite frankly, it's for the benefit of all the parties to have the full context of what we're talking about but I will be happy to sit down with them and work through it, but I don't see the need to break down every page of a book to see the relevance.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm not talking about the page of book, but if you say it is chapter 3 pages so-and-so describing page so-and-so there or chapter describing event there, then that might be of guidance for the Chamber as well, later to consult the -- to look at this evidence in a focussed way. If there's -- if my suggestion -- it is not more than a suggestion could be followed, that would be appreciated.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I think Mr. Misetic's clarification is helpful. I think if we get together quickly we can resolve this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you for your efforts in this respect.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: With respect to the question of -- or actually, let me take you through the break now with a few follow-up questions. It's true, Mr. Mirkovic, at the beginning of your witness statement you said you thought that the Serbian troops were going to defend you, that on the evening of the 4th you saw on the roads and you heard that Serbian forces were on the road and were in fact leaving the area and that given that your -- you thought Serbian forces were going to defend you when you found out that the Serbian forces were evacuating, you decided to evacuate as well. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: SAVA MIRKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir. I did not see those troops. I said that I saw columns moving, but as we set off in the evening, around 9.30 or 10.00, on the way, we were travelling in a passenger vehicle, and we overtook a military truck. That's all. In other words, on the road from Polace -- between Polace and Knin this is where it happened. Whether there were one, two, or three vehicles, I can't really recall anymore because I didn't really pay heed. All I wanted to do at that time was just leave from there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: At paragraph 9 of your 2007 statement, you say that when you got to Serbia the police were directing you to Kosovo. Can you describe what happened when you arrived Serbia, how were they directing you to Kosovo, why, if you know.

utterances.speaker: SAVA MIRKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know, but there was police on the sides of the road and they were directing us where to go, and later on, I learned from people that I met that some of them were directed towards Kosovo, and there were some families who left for Kosovo. Why? I wouldn't know. Perhaps they had accommodations for more people there, or something to that effect.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Well, you say in the statement: I removed my licence plates so the police did not know where I was coming from and left the highway. You removed your licence plates, sir, because you knew that the Serbian authorities wanted you to go to Kosovo. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: SAVA MIRKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I had already realized that they were directing traffic, that they wouldn't allow people to get off the highway. So what did I do, because I had Knin registration plates, I removed the front plate, and then I just got off the road. Nobody really checked me, and maybe it's also because I was lucky there was this good man who wasn't really paying much attention, because were he more weary maybe he wouldn't let me just go on; and that's how I got to Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: What did you think would happen to you if you left the Knin plates on your car?

utterances.speaker: SAVA MIRKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. Some people drove off towards Kosovo, and some found a way - I don't know what way - to remain in Serbia. Serb proper.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Again, my question is what -- what did you think would happen if the plates remained on your car?

utterances.speaker: SAVA MIRKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that moment, I wasn't really thinking, but I had a sister in Belgrade, so all I could think was I should reach my sister where I could find shelter for a while until I found a place where I could live with my family. I wasn't thinking anything really.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Is it safe to say, Mr. Mirkovic, that you thought if you kept the Knin plates on your car that the Serbian authorities wouldn't let you go to Belgrade to your sister's place?

utterances.speaker: SAVA MIRKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this did happen to some people. It didn't happen to me, so this is what I did. I got off the road and I found -- finally I found a way to my sister. To my sister's place. Some people drove towards Kragujevac, Valjevo, Kraljevo, Cacack, but as for Belgrade itself, which is where I managed to get through to, there were all these cars where on the outskirts and they were stopped there, and they weren't allowed to get in.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, there would be a good time for a break. I'm going to change topics.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Misetic could you give us any impression as to what to expect?

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Less than half an hour, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Other parties.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: No questions Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. --

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Depends on Mr. Misetic's questioning. I will probably have half an hour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That means that we will finish most likely within the next session. I can inform the parties I don't know whether the reasons have been communicated already but that the Prosecution has no other witness for this afternoon available. And that matters are uncertain for tomorrow as well. Is that well understood?

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Yes, this is it correct. In fact, it appears that the witness has a serious medical condition and that she will not even be able to testify tomorrow. That's what I just heard.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So the uncertainty appears to develop in the direction of certainty of not being available. We will have a break and we will resume at a quarter past 4.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Misetic, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Mirkovic, in the months prior to Operation Storm, did Mala Polaca have M-77, 128-millimetre rocket systems?

utterances.speaker: SAVA MIRKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about those systems. When I was in the JNA, I was a cook. Therefore, I'm not familiar with these rocket systems.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Did you see anything that would like a rocket system, regardless of whether you could identify the type?

utterances.speaker: SAVA MIRKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about those. The roads that I took, I saw nothing along those.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: You are aware, are you not, of a depot in Polace that housed two T-34 tanks, are you not?

utterances.speaker: SAVA MIRKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I never heard of anything like that in Polace. No depot or anything like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: In June of 1995, you must have seen a check-point that was set up on the Knin-Split road in Polace by the ARSK. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: SAVA MIRKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What year?

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: June 1995.

utterances.speaker: SAVA MIRKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I didn't see that at all. There was no check-point along the road in Polace, not along the Knin road. I took that road every day, or perhaps every third day, but I never saw a check-point there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: From the time the war began in 1991 through Operation Storm, did you hear the sound of rockets being launched from Polace on to Croatian towns, such as Split?

utterances.speaker: SAVA MIRKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I heard nothing from Polace.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'd like to show the witness some documents which I propose that I show as a group and then ask him a few follow-up questions for the sake of efficiency.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Waespi, any objection against the proposed --

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: No, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Registrar, may I please have 1D44-0001.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Mirkovic, what I'm going to do is I'm going to show you a series of documents. You don't have to comment on them at this point unless you feel there is something you feel needs to be clarified. But let me just point out a few things to. This is a Croatian intelligence document dated 7 May 1995. And towards the middle of the page you will see the paragraph says: "On the basis of cooperation with the office for the protection of the constitutional order, Zadar, we obtained the follows information." And the last point is: "Two tanks, T-34, were taken out from the depot in Mala Polaca and they were observed entering the village of Vrlika at the ground position and then the coordinate was identified."

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I tender this and ask that a number be given of to it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Misetic, I see that some text is stricken out. I, of course, first have to see what is stricken out. Usually the Chamber is not --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I will tell you Croatia because it is a security service document produced it to us under their Rule 54 privilege in this way. We don't have any other copy of it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. That's -- that then explains ... let me just read again the portion you just ... Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: I don't know whether I already said we don't have an objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You want numbers to be assigned immediately.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that becomes Exhibit number D723.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D723 -- I'll just write them down and then you put the questions to the witness and then we'll --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: That's fine. I can pose the question simply --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I thought you would provide the series.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: That's fine, I will. Mr. Registrar, if I could have 1D44-0177.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: This is a report, a portion of a report from the Split military district command to the minister of Defence, Minister Susak. You don't have the date on it, but from the text you can see that it is at least as of 7 June 1995, reporting on an UNCRO patrol reported to the superior command in Knin that the Serb forces did not allow the patrolling in the Vrlika area. And then second sentence from the end: "It is noted in the report that all patrols heading from the direction of Knin towards Vrlika are being halted at Mala Polaca check-point."

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I tender this document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: No objections.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that becomes exhibit number D724.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, the next one is 1D44-0179. This is a witness statement given -- or a statement I should just say, a statement dated 9 September 1995 given to the Croatian Ministry of Interior by Slobodan Despanic, who was the company commander of the Vrlika Brigade of the ARSK. It is a long document so we have only taken the portions that are relevant to the issue of Polace. I will skip to the relative portion of this person's statement. He talks about in early 1994 the Zagreb agreement was signed according to which the heavy artillery tanks, Howitzers, and guns were withdrawn to the area of the village of Polace, i.e. approximately 15 kilometres away from the combat line. If we go down on that same page in English, which is page 73 of the B/C/S version. Sorry, it's page 70 of the B/C/S version; I apologise. Back one page, please. The beginning sentence I'm just going to read. It says: "At this time, in the beginning of 1995 from the corps commander in Vrlika Colonel Bozo Kostur and Lieutenant-Colonel Radic arrived from Knin to the forward command post of the brigade," and then it goes on. If we can go to the next paragraph, please. No, I mean, I'm sorry, if we could go back in the English and stay on that page, and the next page in the B/C/S. In the middle of --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I have not received the last line in French or ... I may have missed or mixed up the -- the line, if we can go to the next paragraph and what then appears two lines further down and the next page in B/C/S. It's clear that we move on to the next page in B/C/S --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- and go back to the last page in English. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes, thank you. Towards the middle of that paragraph, it says: "In the area of the village of Polace, in the Lazici hamlet, two T-84 tanks and two transporters had been deployed. Two 88-millimetre coastal guns were deployed in the area of the village of Civljane and Cetina." If we could go to the next page in English and page 74 in the B/C/S, please. Okay. It says: "That night we slept in the house of Vuckovic Momcilo where we listened to the news. On 5 August 1995 at around 1000 hours a woman from Vuckovici came to us and said that combats were ongoing in Knin itself. As we realized that the situation we found ourselves in was hopeless, and having heard the message of President Tudjman on Radio Zagreb, we decided to discard our weapons in the Polace area and we set out carrying a white flag with the aim to surrender. We all wanted to the surrender, except for Mjilkovic Mirko, aka Koca, who threatening us to be traitors, escaped to nearby forest, while Vuckovic Momcilo returned to his house in Polace, saying that he would wait there for the HV soldiers and surrender." And then the bottom of that page in English, and page 75 of the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: In the B/C/S version, sir, at that paragraph that starts [B/C/S spoken], which in English starts at the paragraph when he came to the brigade command in Vrlika, in the middle of that paragraph it says: "He also boasted showing at the map that with the Oganj he had all the targets directly in front of us and that almost all Croatian towns were in the range of the Orkans. The fire on Muc was Split was executed by Zeljko Tisma, yet the names of the other Orkan crew members are unknown to me. The area of Muc and Split are fired at from the Polace area? Your Honour, I ask that this exhibit be marked and tendered into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: I think I have to object to this one unlike the previous documents which were contemporaneous documents on their face had some authentication, this we know it is a gentlemen called Slobodan Despanic, as represented by counsel we don't know who this gentleman is, by whom he was interviewed, we know some kind of Croatian authorities, and so I don't think -- it can be put these parts to the witness and see what he says, but the document itself, a witness statement, I don't think it should be admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I disagree I think I identified Mr. Despanic that he was the company commander in the Vrlika brigade. I gave the date of the statement which means it is contemporaneous as 9 September 1995. I said interviewed by the Croatian MUP.
